justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest downward drift over time, starting near 12.65 for the one-day horizon and gradually declining to around 12.5 at the one-month mark. The near-term estimate was anchored primarily by recent price action and momentum, assuming continuity from whatever the last observed level was. The slight decay in the point estimate over longer horizons reflects a mild mean-reversion assumption — when assets are trading at levels that imply some degree of elevated positioning or stretched sentiment, there is a gentle gravitational pull back toward longer-run equilibrium. The difference between the one-day and one-month estimates is small, however, which signals that I did not have strong directional conviction and was largely expecting the asset to remain range-bound.

The confidence interval widths expand meaningfully as the horizon lengthens, which is a standard feature of forecasting under uncertainty. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly 0.9 units, reflecting relatively constrained overnight variance and the fact that most short-term price moves are modest absent a catalyst. By one week, that span widens to about 1.65 units, incorporating the possibility of scheduled data releases, central bank communications, or idiosyncratic shocks that could accumulate over several trading sessions. At one month, the interval stretches to approximately 3.5 units, capturing the full range of macro developments, positioning shifts, and sentiment changes that could plausibly unfold over that window. Volatility clustering and the possibility of regime changes also contribute to wider long-horizon bands.

Specific risks that could push outcomes beyond my stated intervals include sudden shifts in macroeconomic data — a surprisingly strong or weak inflation print, employment report, or central bank surprise — any of which could generate moves that breach even the outer bounds of my one-week or one-month ranges. Geopolitical events or financial stress in related markets could also produce tail outcomes. On the upside, a sharp reversal in risk sentiment or a short-squeeze dynamic could push prices well above 13.1 even within days. On the downside, a deterioration in liquidity conditions or a broader risk-off episode could drive prices below 10.8 within the month. These are low-probability but non-negligible scenarios that my stated intervals, by construction, give roughly a combined 10% probability to.
